definition: In this historical educational sense, rivalry is a competitive urge to match or outdo another person, especially through imitation. The source describes it as a teaching principle used to spur effort, though it warns that such competition can shift attention away from learning toward personal victory.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Emulation (in education); pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not provide a definition of the term “rivalry” itself; it defines “Emulation (in education)” and mentions “imitative rivalry” as part of that description, so the requested sense of “rivalry” is not directly supported.

The definition’s warning that competition shifts attention “toward personal victory” is not supported by the packet’s wording (the packet instead says emulation should be restricted because it diverts the mind from the real ends of study to “unworthy personal ends,” without mentioning “personal victory”).
